observation_summary: The FastDateParser incorrectly treats whitespace in format strings as a greedy match (\s*+), causing it to accept inputs that SimpleDateFormat would reject. This is a procedural error in the regex generation algorithm.
hypothesis: The FastDateParser class incorrectly implements whitespace handling in its regex generation logic. Specifically, it greedily matches any number of whitespace characters (\s*+) whenever it encounters a single whitespace in the format string, whereas SimpleDateFormat expects a literal or specific whitespace match.
prediction: The regex generation logic in FastDateParser.escapeRegex will contain an unconditional replacement of whitespace with \s*+.
experiment_rationale: The bug report and test failure indicate that FastDateParser is too permissive with whitespace compared to SimpleDateFormat. The fix diff (provided in the oracle) confirms that the logic for handling whitespace was removed/corrected in the escapeRegex method.
reasoning_summary: The defect is a procedural error in how the parser constructs its internal regex representation. By replacing whitespace with a greedy regex match, the algorithm fails to adhere to the expected parsing contract defined by SimpleDateFormat. This is a classic Algorithm/Method defect as it involves the implementation of the parsing logic itself.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix involves changing a condition, the root cause is the implementation of the regex generation algorithm itself, not a missing guard or validation check.
